summary: Post-market: the tape staged a broad comeback in the session after the Fed's first hike since 2023, but the risk model barely moved. Equities rose across the board — every tracked mega-cap gained, led by AMD at 6.6459 percent and MU at 5.5766 percent, with NVDA adding 2.7349 percent — and 21 of 22 tracked sectors and themes finished higher, led by quantum computing at 5.3911 percent, semis leaders at 4.391 percent and memory at 4.202 percent. The fuel was the simultaneous reversal of the two inputs that had driven the sell-off: crude settled lower as Saudi Arabia was reported to offer more supply through Hormuz, and Treasury yields retreated after the Fed and after a Bank of England that left rates unchanged. Credit confirmed the turn, with high-yield spreads at 2.70 from 2.76 and investment-grade at 0.78 from 0.80. The composite nonetheless eased only 1.25 to 46.47 from 47.72 and holds at caution with the regime still goldilocks at a model confidence of 0.9306: the macro block at 63.77 remains the binding constraint, with the 10-year yield at 5.00 and the 10-year real rate at 2.62 both at the 100.0th percentile of their history, and FedWatch still implying 4.15 against an effective funds rate of 3.63. What the rally did not repair is structure: semis relative sits at -16.2669 and small caps at -4.3962, only 5 of 155 names printed a new high, and VIX rose to 17.71 from 17.2 even as equities advanced — the one cross-asset signal that refused to confirm.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The macro block is the binding constraint at 63.77: the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.00 and the 10-year real rate at 2.62 both sit at the 100.0th percentile of their full history, so the discount-rate input has no room left to absorb a hawkish Fed.

Structure is the thinnest part of the rally: semis relative at -16.2669 and small caps at -4.3962 keep leadership narrow, and breadth is only healing from a low base, with the new-highs ratio at 0.0323 against the new-lows ratio at 0.0129.
Volatility refused to confirm the rally: VIX rose to 17.71 from 17.2 while equities advanced, and the volatility dimension deteriorated to 31.46.
The reverse repo facility collapsed to 0.276 from 5.375, pushing that single input to a risk score of 96.47 and flagging scarce reserves even as the tape rallies.

Cross-asset confirmation stayed at 0.5 and contributed 7.5 points, the single largest contribution, yet only 5 of 10 internal signals triggered, with the dollar index at 118.2126 and the real rate at 2.62 both flagging pressure.

supporting_signals.claim: Sector breadth flipped from 8 of 22 positive in the prior session to 21 of 22 today, led by quantum computing at 5.3911 percent, semis leaders at 4.391 percent and memory at 4.202 percent.
Credit improved alongside the tape: high-yield spreads tightened to 2.70 from 2.76 and investment-grade to 0.78 from 0.80.
Breadth is healing from a low base: the share above the 200-day average rose to 0.5677 and the new-highs ratio turned positive at 0.0323.
The chip complex led the recovery: AMD gained 6.6459 percent, MU 5.5766 percent and NVDA 2.7349 percent, with Nvidia guiding that it will sell twice as many chips next year.
Crypto rose with risk appetite: BTC at 76533, up 1.16136 percent, ETH at 2450.53, and SOL at 100.92, up 3.34143 percent.

contradicting_signals.claim: VIX rose to 17.71 even as equities rallied, the clearest non-confirmation of the move.
Cross-asset confirmation is stuck at 0.5, so the model treats the rally as unconfirmed by the full signal set.
The discount rate has no cushion: the 10-year at 5.00 and the real rate at 2.62 are both at the 100.0th percentile, and FedWatch implies 4.15, so the market is still priced for a hike.
Over the longer window the leadership structure has not repaired: semis relative is -16.2669 and small caps -4.3962.
The tracked A-share AI panel diverged from the US tape, closing with 10 of 11 names lower, led by 688825.SH at -2.9583 percent, 301308.SZ at -1.1417 percent and 603986.SH at -0.8737 percent.

what_changed_today: The composite eased 1.25 to 46.47 from 47.72, holding caution and the goldilocks regime.
Equity structure improved to 48.41 and the trend block eased to 45.67, while the volatility block deteriorated to 31.46 from 29.0.
Sector breadth flipped from 8 of 22 positive to 21 of 22.
The new-highs ratio turned positive at 0.0323 after 0.0 in the prior session, and the share above the 200-day average rose to 0.5677.
VIX rose to 17.71 from 17.2 and high-yield spreads tightened to 2.70 from 2.76.
watch_next: Whether the 10-year holds at 5.00 and the real rate at 2.62 — another hot inflation print would push the macro block higher.
The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 and the high-importance Personal Income and Outlays and GDP releases on 2026-09-30.
Whether VIX keeps rising against the tape, which would turn today's non-confirmation into a genuine divergence.
Oil supply headlines around Hormuz, which drove both the crude decline and the yield retreat in this session.
Costco earnings on 2026-09-24 as the first read on the consumer after the hike.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the hike is absorbed and breadth broadens
points: Crude retreats further and the 10-year slips back below 5.00, removing the discount-rate pressure that holds the macro block at 63.77.
Breadth confirms: the share above the 200-day average extends beyond 0.5677 and the new-highs ratio keeps climbing from 0.0323.
Semis relative recovers from -16.2669 as memory and AI hardware earnings confirm the capex cycle.

base_case.title: Base case: goldilocks holds as the tape grinds higher
points: The composite stays in the 45 to 50 band with caution unchanged, as it does at 46.47.
Earnings and the calendar carry the tape; the FOMC on 2026-09-28 passes without pricing a hike beyond 4.15.
Volatility stays elevated but orderly, with VIX oscillating around 17.71.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the discount rate bites and the rally fails
points: The 10-year breaks above 5.00 with the real rate above 2.62, pushing the macro block past 63.77.
VIX keeps rising from 17.71 while equities stall, the non-confirmation turning into a risk-off turn.
Narrow breadth proves decisive: the new-highs ratio at 0.0323 fails to extend and semis relative stays near -16.2669.
